quote.text: I suppose it is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.
quote.author: Abraham Maslow, The Psychology of Science: A Reconnaissance (1966)

stories.kicker: Moscow · the last night of voting
stories.headline: Ukraine sent the largest drone wave of the war at a country that was still counting ballots.
stories.dek: Three official tallies of the same night do not agree. The refinery that burned is sixteen miles from the Kremlin — and Russian refiners, struck seventy times this year, have earned sixteen per cent more than last.

stories.kicker: The invitation · a four-thousand-year-old craft with a recruitment problem
stories.headline: Falconry is the only hobby whose central skill is getting back something you deliberately let go.
stories.dek: Its own recruiters lead with the failure rate: of more than three hundred Californians who start in a typical year, fewer than forty finish.

stories.headline: The root that asks forgiveness now has a spot price.
stories.dek: Fiji’s kava exports have gone from eight million dollars to fifty-three in nine years. Ninety-two per cent of the value in this crop is still domestic — which is precisely why a few hundred bars in Florida can reprice a Fijian village.

stories.kicker: The law · a new offence, and the size of the problem it addresses
stories.headline: From Monday, breaking the casino limit your family asked for can cost you a year.
stories.dek: Over the past decade, between three and fourteen families a year applied for a Family Visit Limit, and about five people a year broke one.

stories.kicker: Barware · the tin, the tension and the fence that got trademarked
stories.headline: A twenty-seven-dollar pair of tins and a hundred-and-sixty-five-dollar pair are the same alloy. Above that you are buying tolerance.
stories.dek: The seal is not made by the metal but by atmospheric pressure and two rims that are round. And the most famous name in the trade will not say where its steel is pressed.

stories.kicker: Hefei · a pitch reached the long way round
stories.headline: China’s memory maker says it is at 11.95 nanometres. It got there without the machine the export controls were written about.
stories.dek: The number is not a node name, and the company has published none of the figures that would let anyone check it. What it does establish is that quadruple patterning went where extreme ultraviolet was supposed to be required.

stories.kicker: Headphones · a very large driver and a very thin sheet
stories.headline: FiiO’s FT15 puts a 101-millimetre planar in walnut, and asks five hundred dollars for it.
stories.dek: The diaphragm is eight hundred nanometres thick — eighty-seven per cent thinner than the model it replaces. At twenty-four ohms it will run off a dongle, which quietly removes the usual second purchase.

stories.kicker: Objects · a dial with no fixed picture
stories.headline: Ressence milled a maze into titanium and then made sure it never sits still.
stories.dek: The discs turn continuously, so the artwork is never twice in the same place — and lines up to show a hidden word only at midnight and midday. Sixty pieces. All gone.

stories.kicker: Music · a record with a short address list
stories.headline: At seventy-nine, Haruomi Hosono made an album and said plainly that it was not meant for us.
stories.dek: “It was intended to be delivered to the people closest to me, sort of like a letter.” His first new material in seven years is also the first this desk has had to review knowing it was addressed elsewhere.

stories.kicker: Schools · a rule that stopped at the classroom door
stories.headline: They banned the phones. A year later, more teenagers were using them in class, not fewer.
stories.dek: Phone use during core lessons rose from 28 to 42 per cent across one school year. Forty-four per cent of students said teachers had got less strict; thirteen per cent of adults had noticed.

stories.kicker: Markets · relief from one side of the ledger only
stories.headline: The ten-year fell five basis points on Monday. The two-year did not move at all.
stories.dek: Oil broke below a hundred dollars because tankers started moving through Hormuz again — and the front end of the curve, which answers to the Fed and not the strait, refused to price a point of it.

stories.kicker: Measurement · the wrong hand on the dynamometer
stories.headline: Being weak predicted nothing. Being lopsided predicted a great deal.
stories.dek: Across 8,132 adults followed for nine years, low grip strength on its own carried a hazard ratio whose confidence interval crossed one. A ten per cent gap between the hands carried 1.23.

stories.kicker: The diary · seventeen days to the street circuit
stories.headline: The three-day grandstands have already gone. Two things on this page close before October does.
stories.dek: Every row was re-checked at a promoter, a venue or an official ticketing page. Three widely-listed items are missing because they have not been announced — see the notes.
